rubrics.rubric: Does the exception table include exactly the 14 non-routine incidents from the watch and exclude the routine medical-only call types?
criterion: The table contains exactly 14 incident rows.
The table excludes all incidents whose type is `Aid Response`, `Nurseline/AMR`, or `Triaged Incident`.

rubrics.rubric: Does every exception row include the required fields, use only the allowed labels, and avoid unsupported unit-level inventions?
criterion: Each row includes incident number, time, address or intersection, incident type, priority tier, likely battalion, most plausible covering station, recommended handling, and a short rationale.
Every priority tier value is one of `immediate life safety`, `urgent`, or `routine/monitor`.
Every recommended handling value is one of `normal dispatch`, `reduced alarm handling`, `special handling/follow-up`, or `coverage watch item`.
The response does not invent unsupported engine, ladder, medic, or battalion-chief unit assignments when the references only support station-level coverage.

rubrics.rubric: Are the core incident facts transcribed accurately enough that the exception table can be trusted operationally?
criterion: F230172376 is shown as a 19:04 `Auto Fire Alarm` at 5941 California Ave Sw.
F230172401 and F230172400 are both shown at 20:03 and keep their correct pairings of address and type: 301 2nd Ave S `Rescue Lock In/Out` and 2614 4th Ave `Automatic Fire Alarm False`.
F230172423 is shown as a 20:49 `Auto Fire Alarm` at 2401 Utah Ave S and is not confused with the separate 20:49 aid call at 3rd Ave / Pine St.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table handle the West Seattle alarm at 5941 California Ave Sw with geographically plausible battalion and station reasoning?
criterion: F230172376 is placed in Battalion 7 or an equivalent West Seattle battalion designation supported by the map.
F230172376 uses Station 32 or Station 37 as the most plausible covering station, or names another immediately adjacent West Seattle station with a clear rationale.
The rationale reflects a West Seattle alarm response context rather than an unrelated downtown or north-end coverage assumption.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table correctly place the north-central incidents around Fremont and Wallingford in plausible Battalion 4 coverage?
criterion: F230172377 at 3636 Francis Ave N is placed in Battalion 4.
F230172377 uses Station 9 as the most plausible covering station, or another immediately adjacent north-central station only if justified.
F230172409 at 1610 N 41st St stays in the same north-central coverage area with Battalion 4 logic and a plausible nearby station such as 9, 17, or 22.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table place the south and southeast exceptions at plausible nearby stations and recognize the far south-end coverage draw?
criterion: F230172378 at 5829 16th Ave S uses Station 27 or Station 13 and stays in plausible south or southeast battalion coverage.
F230172382 at 3104 34th Ave S uses Station 30 as the most plausible covering station.
F230172411 at 10721 66th Ave S uses Station 33 as the most plausible covering station and recognizes the far south-end location.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table correctly place the north and northeast incidents in Battalion 6 with plausible nearby station coverage?
criterion: F230172387 at 3010 NE 113th St is assigned to Battalion 6 with Station 39 or Station 40 as the most plausible cover.
F230172408 at 12020 31st Ave NE is assigned to Battalion 6 with Station 39 or Station 40 as the most plausible cover.
F230172397 at 1420 NE 65th St is assigned to Battalion 6 with Station 16 or Station 17 as the most plausible cover.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table give the central, downtown, and SODO exceptions plausible nearby station coverage?
criterion: F230172391 at 3417 S King St uses a plausible nearby central or south station such as Station 6 or Station 30.
F230172401 at 301 2nd Ave S uses SFD HQ or Station 10 as the most plausible covering station.
F230172400 at 2614 4th Ave uses Station 2 as the most plausible covering station.
F230172423 at 2401 Utah Ave S uses Station 14 as the most plausible covering station.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table correctly place the Ballard-area residential alarm in plausible Battalion 4 coverage?
criterion: F230172422 at 2649 NW 56th St is placed in Battalion 4.
F230172422 uses Station 18 as the most plausible covering station, or another immediately adjacent Ballard-area station only if justified.

rubrics.rubric: Does the table distinguish true life-safety or hazard calls from lower-acuity exception items when assigning priority tiers?
criterion: F230172378 `Activated CO Detector` is not labeled `routine/monitor`.
F230172411 `Medic Response- 7 per Rule` is treated as at least `urgent` and preferably `immediate life safety`.
Lower-acuity items such as F230172400 `Automatic Fire Alarm False` or F230172401 `Rescue Lock In/Out` are not overstated as `immediate life safety` without a specific reason.

rubrics.rubric: Do the handling recommendations fit the actual incident types instead of collapsing everything into one dispatch disposition?
criterion: Auto alarms, alarm bells, and residential alarm activations are generally handled as `normal dispatch` or `reduced alarm handling`, not as blanket `special handling/follow-up` items.
F230172408 `Investigate Out Of Service` is treated as `special handling/follow-up` or `coverage watch item` rather than a routine closeout.
High-acuity or hazardous calls such as F230172378 or F230172411 are not relegated to `routine/monitor` handling.

rubrics.rubric: Are the row rationales incident-specific, operationally meaningful, and honest about uncertainty where the references are not exact?
criterion: The rationales cite concrete reasons such as CO hazard, residential alarm uncertainty, out-of-service infrastructure concern, illegal burn exposure, or south-end ALS demand.
The rationales distinguish dispatch priority from coverage significance when those are not the same thing.
The rationales do not merely repeat the incident type with no additional judgment.
When battalion or station certainty is limited by the references, the rationale acknowledges that the assignment is the most plausible choice rather than a confirmed dispatch.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response deliver exactly the requested turnover products and keep the handoff note concise instead of turning it into a second table?
criterion: The response contains one exception table and one separate supervisor handoff note.
The note is between 250 and 350 words.
The note summarizes the two-hour watch rather than listing every incident one by one.
The note explicitly frames routine medical activity as the background workload affecting coverage.

rubrics.rubric: Does the handoff note describe the watch volume and call mix accurately enough to support supervisory judgment?
criterion: The note recognizes that the watch contained 35 total incidents, or provides an equivalently accurate summary of a heavy two-hour volume.
The note distinguishes the 14 exception incidents from the larger routine medical queue.
The note makes clear that Aid Response, Nurseline/AMR, and Triaged Incident volume still mattered for coverage even though those calls were excluded from the exception table.

rubrics.rubric: Does the handoff note identify meaningful geographic clustering that could affect coverage on the next watch and connect it to operational consequences?
criterion: The note identifies at least one north or northeast cluster affecting Battalion 6 coverage.
The note identifies at least one south, southeast, or downtown cluster affecting central or south coverage.
The note connects clustering to potential backfill, station availability, or coverage-watch implications.

rubrics.rubric: Does the handoff note flag the most important non-routine incidents for carryover attention?
criterion: The note flags F230172378 or the CO-detector hazard at 5829 16th Ave S for carryover awareness.
The note flags F230172408 or the out-of-service investigation at 12020 31st Ave NE as a follow-up or coverage issue.
The note flags F230172411 or the high-acuity far south-end medic response as a carryover resource concern.
